# Summary {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
# Estimates come from scripts/03_fit_models.R, the same ones the chapters use.
by30 <- results$by30
or30 <- results$or30
or_marginal <- results$or_marginal
by_time <- results$by_time
lasts <- results$lasts
```

**Question.** Does gargling licorice before intubation reduce postoperative
sore throat compared with a sugar-water gargle?

**Answer.** Yes, in this trial. Thirty minutes after arrival in recovery,
`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Licorice"])` of licorice patients
reported any sore throat at rest, against
`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Sugar"])` of sugar-water patients
(`r fmt_or(or30)`; `r fmt_p(or30$p_value)`). `r if (lasts) "The effect lasted:" else "Whether the effect lasted is unclear:"`
population-averaged odds ratios at the four assessments through the first
postoperative morning ranged from `r fmt_num(min(by_time$or), 2)` to
`r fmt_num(max(by_time$or), 2)`, and `r if (lasts) "all" else "not all"` of
their confidence intervals excluded one (assuming one common effect,
`r fmt_or(or_marginal)`).

**How to read this book.** It is both the lab notebook and the report. The
*Plan* part was written before the results; the *Results* part follows it;
the *Record* part holds every analysis decision and the research log. Every
number in the Plan and Results prose is computed by code: the models are
fitted once by `scripts/03_fit_models.R`, and the text formats those
results when the book renders, so it cannot drift from the analysis;
`make numbers` checks this. The decision record and research log are hand-written logs, and say
so.

::: {.callout-note}
## This is a teaching example
The data are the public licorice gargle trial (Ruetzler et al., *Anesth
Analg* 2013), distributed in the `medicaldata` R package. The "client" and
the engagement are fictional; the analysis is real.
:::
